content: The number of mosquitoes capable of flying or walking is recorded to adjust for the total mosquito sample size available to respond to the active ingredient (AI) in each replicate. The butterfly valves are opened for 10 minutes to allow chemical vapors to flow through the test unit and to enable free movement of mosquitoes throughout the unit, as indicated by the grey arrows in the schematic. After 10 minutes, the gates are closed, and the number of mosquitoes in each cylinder is recorded. Additionally, the number of knocked-down mosquitoes in each cylinder is documented. All mosquitoes are kept overnight to assess 24-hour mortality. If mortality is significantly higher than in the controls, the insecticidal activity must be evaluated according to established WHO efficacy guidelines. Between replicates, the metal cylinders are disconnected from the clear cylinders, and the end cap is removed from the control metal cylinder for 3 minutes to allow passive ventilation of the AI from the clear and control metal cylinders before the next replicate. During this ventilation period, all treated substrates remain in place within the metal cylinders under the chemical hood. Successive replicates are conducted without delay. At the end of each evaluation, the cylinders are washed. The metal components are cleaned with acetone solution and non-fragrant laboratory detergent solution. All component sections are allowed to dry overnight before reuse for testing other AIs or dosages. Nine replicates are performed for each AI dosage. At the conclusion of testing, the proportion of mosquitoes repelled by the treatment is determined. Spatial repellency is expressed as the proportion of mosquitoes prevented from entering the treatment space relative to all mosquitoes moving within the system, calculated using the spatial activity index (SAI). The SAI is calculated as follows: [ SAI = frac{(Nc Nt)}{(Nc + Nt)} times frac{Nm}{N} ] Where: ( SAI ) is the spatial activity index. ( Nc ) is the number of mosquitoes in the control metal chamber. ( Nt ) is the number of mosquitoes in the treatment metal chamber. ( Nm ) is the total number of mosquitoes in the two metal chambers. ( N ) is the total number of mosquitoes in the test unit. The SAI ranges from -1 to 1: A value of 0 indicates no response. A value of -1 indicates all mosquitoes moved into the treatment chamber, showing an attractant response. A value of 1 indicates all mosquitoes moved into the control chamber, showing a spatial repellent response. If no mosquitoes are present in either chamber (( Nt = 0, Nc = 0 )), the test is valid, but the SAI is 0. The SAI is calculated for each replicate, and the mean index for each AI dosage is analyzed using probit-plane regression analysis to estimate the ED50 and ED95 values with corresponding 95% confidence limits. The number of replicates, total number of mosquitoes, and mean SAI (± standard error) for each AI dosage and negative control should be reported. The objective of the host attraction-inhibition test is to measure the ability of an AI to inhibit mosquito attraction to a host. This is achieved using a Y-tube olfactometer to measure attraction to host odors in the absence and presence of the AI. The Y-tube olfactometer consists of a central base leg made of acrylic plastic, which forms the main body. Two branches meet the base leg at a decision point. Each branch has a trapping port with a mesh screen over the end, and each trapping port has a rotating circular door with a mesh screen. The mesh allows odors from the air input to pass through while preventing direct contact between mosquitoes and odor sources. During a test, odors migrate down the branches, through the base leg, and to the holding port, from which test mosquitoes are released. Environmental conditions (e.g., temperature and humidity) should be recorded and maintained consistently across tests. A preliminary test with diluent only at one port should be conducted to ensure no response to the solvent (indicated by an attraction response ≤ 10%). Serial dilutions of the AI are prepared with methanol (or another suitable diluent) and tested to identify the effective dose range. Dosages eliciting responses between 10% and 95% are used for analysis, with at least two or three dosages inducing attraction responses >50% and the remaining dosages inducing attraction <50%. A pipette is used to deliver 400 µL of the repellent AI solution or diluent to a 9-mm vial cap. Both control (diluent only) and treatment (AI and diluent) vial caps are placed in position in the end caps and attached to the trapping ports before testing. The olfactometer operates with airflow in a chemical hood equipped with vacuum and air lines to provide airflow. Mosquitoes are introduced into the holding port and allowed to acclimatize to the test environment with clean air for 15 minutes. Damaged mosquitoes incapable of flying or walking are excluded, and only those capable of responding are observed and recorded. The total number of mosquitoes in the treatment trapping port, control trapping port, and outside these ports is recorded. Between replicates, the end caps and trapping ports are disconnected from the Y-tube branches, and the unit is passively cleaned with airflow for at least 3 minutes under the chemical hood to clear odors before the next replicate. All traps remain in place during the ventilation period. Successive replicates are conducted by repeating the process of loading a new trap with 10 mosquitoes and allowing them to acclimatize. The Y-tube body and individual trapping ports are washed at the end of each chemical evaluation using non-fragrant laboratory detergent solution. All parts are allowed to dry overnight before reuse. A minimum of six replicates is performed for each AI dosage. At the end of testing, the proportion of mosquitoes attracted to the treatment is determined. The percentage attraction to the treatment port is calculated by dividing the number of mosquitoes trapped in the treatment port by the total number of mosquitoes in the test (excluding damaged mosquitoes). The mean percentage attraction is calculated from the responses of the six replicates to each treatment. The percentage attraction for each AI dosage is determined using probit-plane regression analysis to estimate the ED50 and ED95 values with corresponding 95% confidence limits. The number of replicates, total number of mosquitoes, and mean percentage attraction (± standard error) for each AI dosage and negative control should be reported. The objective of spatial repellency studies is to determine differences in spatial repellency between insecticide-susceptible and insecticide-resistant strains to inform disease protection and control strategies. The protective efficacy of formulated products is assessed to determine the optimal dosage and duration of protective efficacy in a treated space under controlled conditions. Protective efficacy is measured by the difference in landing or feeding inhibition between treated groups and controls over time. Products are evaluated in a free-flight room according to label instructions. Efficacy is assessed from a minimum of four replicates with 50 mosquitoes for both treatment and control. Comparison with a standard product or positive control is necessary. The duration of protective efficacy is measured by collecting data at various times after product activation. Products should be stored according to label claims between evaluations under conditions similar to those during testing. Longer-lasting products can be experimentally aged in environmental chambers before testing. Free-flight rooms should be mosquito-proof, well-ventilated, and equipped with an extraction fan to clear vapors between tests. Rooms should measure 30 m³ with smooth, light-colored surfaces for easy cleaning and visibility of mosquitoes. Environmental conditions should be maintained at 27 ± 2°C and 80% ± 10% relative humidity during testing. Biological efficacy is assessed at several time points until it falls below 50%. Mosquitoes are acclimatized for 1 hour under conditions similar to the test space before release. If human landing catch is measured, mosquitoes are collected continuously for 1 hour. If feeding inhibition is measured, blood-fed mosquitoes are collected by aspiration at the end of the test. Landing inhibition and feeding inhibition percentages are calculated using the respective equations. Data should include test duration, protective efficacy duration, number of replicates, and mean percentage inhibition with 95% confidence intervals. Room size and distance between the spatial repellent source and the human should also be reported.
